source.title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a finite set P of points in the plane whose visibility graph is exactly G, where two points of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a set of points P in the plane.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 Characterize visibility graphs of point sets.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Given the visibility graph G of a set of points, draw the points in the plane whose visibility graph is G.

accepted.question_text: Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Prove that every visibility graph with omega(G) <= 4 has chi(G) <= 5.

accepted.question_text: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Prove Conjecture 1 for visibility graphs with omega(G) = 5.

accepted.question_text: For integers k >= 2 and ell >= 2, every sufficiently large planar point set should contain either ell collinear points or k mutually visible points. Prove this in the remaining open cases k = 6 or ell = 4.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Prove Conjecture 2 for k = 6 or ell = 4.

accepted.question_text: Let b(P) be the minimum size of a blocking set Q for a finite point set P in general position, and let b(n) be the minimum of b(P) over all n-point sets with no three points collinear. Prove that b(n)/n tends to infinity as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 Prove that as n -> infinity, b(n) / n -> infinity.

accepted.question_text: Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8 Is the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices bounded above by a linear function of n?

accepted.question_text: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Improve the present lower bound O(n/ log2 n) of the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices.

accepted.question_text: For each integer h > 1, determine the smallest number of vertices that a graph can have while having obstacle number exactly h.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10 For h > 1, what is the smallest number of vertices of a graph with obstacle number h?

accepted.question_text: Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Does every planar graph have obstacle number 1?

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a set S of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G, where vertices correspond to segment endpoints and two endpoints are adjacent when the segment joining them avoids all segments of S, with the two endpoints of each original segment also adjacent.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the segment visibility graph of a set of disjoint segments S in the plane.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as segment visibility graphs of finite collections of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Characterize the segment visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be a segment visibility graph, construct a set of pairwise disjoint line segments in the plane whose segment visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Given a segment visibility graph G, draw the segments S in the plane whose visibility graph is G.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, find a Hamiltonian cycle of G in polynomial time.
accepted.context_brief: Hamiltonian cycles in segment visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify a Hamiltonian cycle in G in polynomial time.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a segment visibility graph G, identify which edges of G correspond to the original segments of the underlying segment set S.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 16 Given a segment visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, identify the edges of G that correspond to segments of S.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs admit a unit bar visibility representation, meaning a bar visibility representation in which all horizontal bars have the same length.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 17 Characterize unit bar visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Is recognizing unit bar visibility graphs an NP-complete problem?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 18 Is recognition of unit bar visibility graphs NP-complete?

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs are bar k-visibility graphs, where vertices are horizontal bars and two bars are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment between them intersects at most k other bars.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 19 Characterize bar k-visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Triangle-free non-planar graphs are already known to be forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Determine whether there are other classes of forbidden subgraphs for bar k-visibility graphs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 20 Triangle-free non-planar graphs are forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs. Is there any other class of forbidden subgraphs of bar k-visibility graphs?

accepted.question_text: For k >= 5, determine whether there exist (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21 Are there (2k + 2)-regular bar k-visibility graphs for k >= 5?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist d-regular bar k-visibility graphs with degree d >= 2k + 3.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 22 Are there d-regular bar k-visibility graphs with d >= 2k + 3?

accepted.question_text: Improve the current upper bound 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic number of bar k-visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 23 Improve the current upper bound of 6k + 6 on the chromatic number of a bar k-visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: The thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is known to be at most 2k(9k - 1). Improve this upper bound.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 24 It has been shown that the thickness of a bar k-visibility graph is bounded by 2k(9k - 1). Can this upper bound be improved?

accepted.question_text: What is the largest possible crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?
accepted.context_brief: Crossing numbers of bar k-visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 25 The crossing number of a graph is the minimum possible number of crossings with which the graph can be drawn in the plane. What is the largest crossing number of a bar k-visibility graph?

accepted.question_text: What is the largest possible genus of a bar k-visibility graph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 26 The genus of a graph is the minimal integer g such that the graph can be embedded on a surface of genus g. What is the largest genus of a bar k-visibility graph?

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs are rectangle visibility graphs, where vertices are isothetic rectangles with pairwise disjoint interiors and two vertices are adjacent exactly when their rectangles are horizontally or vertically visible by an unobstructed beam of finite width.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 27 Characterize rectangle visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G, determine whether there exists a simple polygon P whose vertex visibility graph is G, where two vertices of P are adjacent exactly when the segment joining them lies entirely inside P.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 28 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P .

accepted.question_text: Is the problem of recognizing whether a graph is the visibility graph of a simple polygon in NP?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 29 Is the problem of recognizing visibility graphs in NP ?

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a graph G together with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary order is exactly the cycle C.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 30 Given a graph G in adjacency matrix form along with a Hamiltonian cycle C of G, determine whether G is the visibility graph of a simple polygon P whose boundary corresponds to the given Hamiltonian cycle C.

accepted.question_text: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of simple polygons.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 32 Characterize visibility graphs of simple polygons.

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a simple polygon, construct a simple polygon whose visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 33 Draw a simple polygon whose visibility graph is the given graph G.

accepted.question_text: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P, determine which Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponds to the boundary of P.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 34 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P , determine the Hamiltonian cycle in G that corresponds to the boundary of P .

accepted.question_text: Design a constant-factor approximation algorithm for the minimum dominating set problem on visibility graphs of simple polygons.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 35 Design a constant factor approximation algorithm for computing minimum dominating set of visibility graphs.

accepted.question_text: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum hidden sets with boundary order

evidence.quote: Open Problem 36 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P along with the Hamiltonian cycle in G corresponding to the boundary of P , determine the maximum hidden set of G.

accepted.question_text: Design an approximation algorithm for computing a maximum hidden set in a visibility graph.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 37 Design an approximation algorithm for computing maximum hidden set of visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: Given the adjacency matrix of a visibility graph G, compute a maximum clique of G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 38 Given a visibility graph G in adjacency matrix form, compute a maximum clique of G.

accepted.question_text: Improve the current lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons with n vertices.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 40 Improve the lower and upper bounds on the number of non-isomorphic visibility graphs of simple polygons.

accepted.question_text: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 41 Can all endpoints of a visibility graph be assigned integer coordinates such that the integers use a polynomial number of bits?

accepted.question_text: Determine the correct asymptotic order of the minimum number of bits needed by an optimal covering-set representation of a visibility graph, where a covering set is a family of cliques and complete bipartite graphs whose members are subgraphs of the visibility graph and whose union covers every edge.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 42 Give a tight bound (with respect to order notation) on the number of bits used in an optimal covering set of a visibility graph.

accepted.question_text: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 43 Find a covering set which matches the above bound in polynomial time.

accepted.question_text: For each integer k, does there exist an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points? Here a k-blocked point set is a set of planar points colored with k colors so that mutually visible points receive different colors and points that are not visible because of collinear blockers receive the same color.
accepted.context_brief: Bounded size of k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 For each integer k, there is an integer n such that every k-blocked point set has at most n points.

accepted.question_text: Does every k-blocked point set have O(k^2) points?
accepted.context_brief: Quadratic bound for k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4 Every k-blocked point set has O(k^2 ) points.

accepted.question_text: In every k-blocked point set, must each color class contain at most k points?
accepted.context_brief: Color-class size in k-blocked point sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5 In every k-blocked point set, there are at most k points in each colour class.

accepted.question_text: Does every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) have vertex-connectivity at least (2 delta(G) + 1) / 3?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6 Every visibility graph G with minimum degree delta(G) has vertex-connectivity at least (2delta(G)+1)/3.

accepted.question_text: For point visibility graphs G, is the chromatic number χ(G) bounded above by some function of the clique number ω(G)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1 There exists a function f such that χ(G) ≤ f(ω(G)).
For visibility graphs with ω(G) ≥ 6, Pfender [91] proved that the conjecture does not hold as shown in the following lemma.

accepted.question_text: For all integers k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, does there exist an integer h(k, ℓ) such that every planar point set of at least h(k, ℓ) points contains either ℓ collinear points or k mutually visible points?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Prove Conjecture 2 for k = 6 or ℓ = 4.

accepted.question_text: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7 Every segment visibility graph G contains a Hamiltonian cycle C.
Since Conjectures 8 is true, Conjectures 7 is also true.

accepted.question_text: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle that becomes a non-self-intersecting Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph?
accepted.context_brief: Hamiltonian circuits in embedded segment visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8 Every segment visibility graph G contains a Hamiltonian cycle C that corresponds to a Hamiltonian circuit in the embedded segment visibility graph G′.

Later, Conjectures 8 was proved for all classes of segments in S by Hoffmann and Tóth [65] using the result of Bose et al. [15], and they presented an O(n log n) time algorithm for locating a Hamiltonian circuit in G′.

accepted.question_text: Does every segment visibility graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle whose embedding is the boundary of a circumscribing polygon?
accepted.context_brief: Circumscribing polygons for segment visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9 Every segment visibility graph G contains a Hamiltonian cycle C that corresponds to the boundary of a circumscribing polygon in the embedded segment visibility graph G′.
However, Urbe and Watanabe [114] gave a counter-example to Conjecture 9.

accepted.question_text: In the embedded segment visibility graph G′ of a set S of n disjoint segments, is there always an alternating path containing at least O(log n) segments of S?
accepted.context_brief: Alternating paths in embedded segment visibility graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10 In the embedded segment visibility graph G′ of a set S of n disjoint segments, there exists an alternating path containing at least O(log n) segments of S.
Urratia [115] made the following conjecture which was proved by Hoffmann and Tóth [64].

needs_review.question_text_raw: Open Problem 39 Determine whether a set of vertices of a visibility graph has a triangle-extendible ordering in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Spinrad [106] has discussed possible approaches for computing maximum clique using the notion of triangle-extendible ordering which is essentially a transitive orientation of the graph.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Open Problem 31 Design an algorithm for testing Necessary Condition 4 in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 31 Design an algorithm for testing Necessary Condition 4 in polynomial time.

trace.notes: Mapped the paper into point, segment, and polygon visibility sections and identified the enumerated problem regions.
Extracted point-visibility open problems and conjectures, including coloring, blockers, obstacles, and connectivity items.
Extracted segment-visibility, unit-bar, bar-k, and rectangle-visibility problems.
Extracted polygon-visibility problems on recognition, characterization, reconstruction, optimization, counting, and representation.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/1012.5187.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
